intent.raw_query: New Zealand South Island, $4000, hiking and bungee jumping, November 2026

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Take the ultimate leap from New Zealand's highest bungy jump at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. This iconic AJ Hackett experience offers breathtaking views of the Remarkables mountain range and an adrenaline rush like no other. The jump includes a scenic gondola ride to the suspended pod over the canyon.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Multi-Day Hike
experiences.description: Trek one of New Zealand's Great Walks through pristine alpine scenery connecting Fiordland and Mount Aspiring National Parks. The 32km trail features dramatic mountain passes, glacier-carved valleys, and stunning views of Lake Mackenzie. Huts are available along the route for overnight stays, making it perfect for a 2-3 day adventure.

experiences.name: Franz Josef Glacier Valley Walk
experiences.description: Hike through the dramatic terminal valley of Franz Josef Glacier, one of the world's most accessible glaciers descending into a temperate rainforest. The self-guided valley walk takes you to stunning glacier viewpoints with towering ice walls and turquoise meltwater streams. Rangers provide safety briefings and the trail is well-marked with multiple lookout points.

experiences.name: Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo
experiences.description: Paddle through the majestic fiords of Milford Sound while surrounded by towering peaks, cascading waterfalls, and abundant wildlife including dolphins and seals. Combine the kayaking experience with a guided walk along the Milford foreshore track for a full day of immersive nature adventure. The experience includes equipment, guides, and stunning views of Mitre Peak.

experiences.name: Ben Lomond Summit Hike
experiences.description: Conquer the iconic Ben Lomond peak rising 1748 meters above Queenstown for panoramic views of Lake Wakatipu, the Remarkables, and surrounding mountain ranges. The challenging 11km return trail begins through beech forest before opening into dramatic alpine terrain above the treeline. Take the Skyline Gondola up to shorten the ascent and save energy for the summit push.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - New Zealand South Island
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Franz Josef Glacier Valley Walk
experiences.description: Hike through the dramatic terminal valley of Franz Josef Glacier, one of the world's most accessible glaciers descending into a temperate rainforest. The self-guided valley walk takes you to stunning glacier viewpoints with towering ice walls and turquoise meltwater streams. Rangers provide safety briefings and the trail is well-marked with multiple lookout points.

experiences.name: Ben Lomond Summit Hike
experiences.description: Conquer the iconic Ben Lomond peak rising 1748 meters above Queenstown for panoramic views of Lake Wakatipu, the Remarkables, and surrounding mountain ranges. The challenging 11km return trail begins through beech forest before opening into dramatic alpine terrain above the treeline. Take the Skyline Gondola up to shorten the ascent and save energy for the summit push.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Queenstown Airport at 13:00. Collect luggage, grab a local SIM card, and take the Orbus public bus (Route 1, ~$10 NZD) into Queenstown town centre. Check in to Nevis Valley, Queenstown Boutique Stay. Take a relaxed walk along the Queenstown Bay lakefront promenade to get your bearings — free and scenic.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Queenstown's compact town centre. Browse the waterfront and watch the sunset over The Remarkables mountain range from Queenstown Gardens (free entry). Grab a cheap dinner and rest up after the long flight.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport on arrival
meals.lunch: Fergburger is iconic but pricey — opt for a $10–12 NZD wrap or pie from a local bakery like Vudu Café or a supermarket (New World on Beach Street)
meals.dinner: Countdown or New World supermarket meal prep or $15 NZD budget bowl from Mama's Fish House takeaway

day_by_day.notes: Priority on Day 1: buy a 7-day Orbus bus pass if planning to use public transport, stock up on groceries at New World for self-catering breakfasts and snacks throughout the trip. Exchange currency or use a no-fee travel card (Wise recommended).

day_by_day.morning: Early start for the Ben Lomond Summit Hike — one of the South Island's most rewarding day hikes. Take the Skyline Gondola ($40 NZD one-way, or hike up from town for free via the Ben Lomond Track from Lomond Crescent). Begin the summit trail from the Gondola top station. The hike to the summit (1,748m) takes approximately 4–5 hours return from the top station.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Ben Lomond Summit Hike — reach the summit for breathtaking 360-degree panoramic views over Lake Wakatipu, Queenstown, and The Remarkables. Descend back to the Gondola station or all the way to town on foot (saves $40 NZD gondola descent cost). Pack a homemade lunch to eat at the summit.
day_by_day.evening: Soak tired legs at the free Queenstown waterfront area. Visit the Queenstown Night Markets (Monday nights, Earnslaw Park) for affordable street food from $5–10 NZD per dish — great variety and lively atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered oats or toast at accommodation before the hike
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from supermarket — sandwiches, trail mix, fruit, and plenty of water for the summit hike
meals.dinner: Queenstown Night Markets — try dumplings, curries, or wood-fired pizza from $8–12 NZD per serving

day_by_day.notes: Ben Lomond Summit Hike is a Grade 4 hike — wear sturdy footwear, bring sunscreen, layers, and at least 2L of water per person. Weather can change rapidly at altitude. Check the MetService NZ forecast the night before. Total hike from town and back is approximately 11km and 1,400m elevation gain — allow a full day.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning after the Ben Lomond summit. Sleep in and enjoy a slow self-catered breakfast. Visit the Queenstown Gardens (free) for a gentle morning walk through the rose gardens and lakeside paths — great for stretching sore legs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the free Frankton Arm walking/cycling trail along the lake edge toward Kelvin Heights (approximately 5km one way). Enjoy views of The Remarkables reflected in Lake Wakatipu. Alternatively, visit the free Kiwi Birdlife Park viewing areas near the gondola base (full entry is $49 NZD but the surrounding trails are free).
day_by_day.evening: Head into town for a budget dinner. Explore the free art installations along the Queenstown waterfront. Watch the TSS Earnslaw steam ship depart from the wharf (free to watch from shore).

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — eggs on toast, yoghurt and fruit at accommodation
meals.lunch: Grab a $5–7 NZD pie or sausage roll from Queenstown Bakery or Pak'nSave supermarket
meals.dinner: Winnies Pizza (happy hour deals ~$15 NZD) or self-catered pasta at accommodation

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberate recovery day — Ben Lomond is physically demanding and your legs will thank you. Use this time to plan logistics for the Franz Josef portion of the trip and book any shuttles in advance for better pricing.

day_by_day.morning: Bungee jumping day — book the Kawarau Bridge Bungy (43m, the world's first commercial bungy site) with AJ Hackett. This is the most budget-friendly bungy option in the Queenstown area at approximately $175–195 NZD. Arrive early for your booked time slot. The Kawarau Bridge is 23km from Queenstown (take the Nomad Safaris shuttle or join a group transfer ~$15 NZD return).
day_by_day.afternoon: After the adrenaline rush, walk the free Kawarau Gorge Suspension Bridge viewing area and surrounding short trails. Return to Queenstown and visit the free Queenstown Museum on Ballarat Street to learn about the region's gold rush history.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your bungy jump! Head to Searle Lane for budget-friendly bars. Try The World Bar for cheap cocktails and a lively backpacker atmosphere. Watch your spending — set a $20 NZD drinks budget.

meals.breakfast: Light self-catered breakfast before the jump — don't eat too heavily before bungying
meals.lunch: Pack snacks for Kawarau Gorge or grab a $10 NZD burger from the Kawarau Bridge café
meals.dinner: Ferg Bakery (cheaper sibling of Fergburger) for $10–14 NZD burgers or wraps

day_by_day.notes: Book Kawarau Bridge Bungy at least 2–3 days in advance online for the best pricing and time slot availability. Wear comfortable clothes with no loose items. Video packages are an additional cost (~$50 NZD) — decide in advance if it's worth it for the memory. Weight limits apply (45–180kg).

day_by_day.morning: Depart Queenstown early for the drive/shuttle to Wanaka (approximately 1 hour via Crown Range Road — New Zealand's highest sealed road). If not renting a car, take the Ritchies/Intercity coach (~$20–30 NZD). Arrive in Wanaka and walk the free Wanaka lakefront promenade. Visit the famous Wanaka Tree (lone willow in the lake) — free and iconic photo stop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Mount Iron Loop Track (1.5 hours, 240m elevation gain) — completely free and offers stunning views over Lake Wanaka, Lake Hawea, and surrounding peaks. This is a well-marked, moderate track starting right from the town edge.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown via the same shuttle/coach, or if this is a transit day toward Franz Josef, continue north. Enjoy dinner in Wanaka before returning or departing.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation before departing Queenstown
meals.lunch: Wanaka Bakpaka café or supermarket — $8–12 NZD sandwich and snack
meals.dinner: Kai Whakapai Café & Bar in Wanaka for affordable meals, or self-catered back at Queenstown accommodation

day_by_day.notes: Wanaka is a beautiful day trip from Queenstown. If budget allows, consider staying one night in Wanaka (Wanaka Backpacker Hostel ~$35–40 NZD/night) to break up the journey north toward Franz Josef. The Crown Range Road offers spectacular views but can be challenging in poor weather — check conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Queenstown/Wanaka to Franz Josef Glacier. This is a long journey (~5–6 hours by road). Take the Intercity coach or Naked Bus (~$45–70 NZD booked in advance) via Haast Pass — one of New Zealand's most scenic drives through UNESCO World Heritage rainforest. Depart early (7:00–8:00am) to maximise daylight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Franz Josef township early-to-mid afternoon. Check in to budget accommodation (Franz Josef YHA or Rainforest Retreat camping/dorm ~$35–45 NZD/night). Walk the free Sentinel Rock Lookout Track (20 minutes return) for your first dramatic view of the glacier valley.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the small Franz Josef township. Visit the free DOC (Department of Conservation) visitor centre to learn about the glacier's history and get trail maps for tomorrow. Enjoy a quiet evening in preparation for the big glacier walk.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast at Queenstown accommodation before departing
meals.lunch: Pack snacks and sandwiches for the coach journey — there are limited food stops en route
meals.dinner: Alice May Restaurant in Franz Josef has budget options, or self-cater at the hostel kitchen — Franz Josef is remote so supermarket options are limited (Four Square store available but pricier)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Intercity/Naked Bus Franz Josef route well in advance — seats sell out, especially in November (peak season). The Haast Pass road is stunning but can close in extreme weather. Franz Josef township is very small — the Four Square supermarket is expensive, so pack as many supplies as possible from Queenstown's New World before departing.

day_by_day.morning: Early start for the Franz Josef Glacier Valley Walk — the highlight of the West Coast. Begin the free DOC-maintained Glacier Valley Walk from the car park (2km from town — walk or bike). The track winds through dramatic terminal moraine, ancient rainforest, and braided glacial rivers. The walk to the glacier viewing platform takes approximately 1.5–2 hours return.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the glacier valley. Walk the Roberts Point Track (4–5 hours return, more challenging) for elevated views of the glacier face and ice falls — completely free. Alternatively, take the shorter Alex Knob Track partial walk through beautiful podocarp rainforest.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Franz Josef township. Visit the free Waiho River bridge viewpoint at dusk for golden-hour glacier views. Relax and share stories with fellow travellers at the hostel.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast at hostel — oats, toast, and coffee before hitting the trail
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten in the glacier valley — sandwiches, trail mix, energy bars, and plenty of water
meals.dinner: Self-catered at hostel kitchen or $15–18 NZD meal at Monsoon Bar & Restaurant in Franz Josef

day_by_day.notes: The Franz Josef Glacier Valley Walk is FREE and one of New Zealand's most accessible glacier experiences — do not pay for a guided walk if budget is tight. However, you cannot walk onto the glacier itself without a paid guide (glacier access has been restricted due to retreat and safety). Sandflies (biting insects) are intense in this area — bring strong insect repellent. Wear waterproof layers as the West Coast receives very high rainfall.

day_by_day.morning: Explore more of the Franz Josef area. Hike the free Lake Wombat Track (1 hour return) through ancient kahikatea forest to a beautiful hidden lake — one of the area's hidden gems. Alternatively, walk the Tatare Tunnels Track (1.5 hours return) through a historic gold mining tunnel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the free Waiho Gorge viewpoint walk. If weather is poor (common on the West Coast), visit the DOC visitor centre for educational displays, or relax and warm up at the hostel. Consider driving or shuttling 25km north to Fox Glacier township for the free Fox Glacier Valley Walk for a second glacier perspective.
day_by_day.evening: Pack bags and prepare for tomorrow's travel day. Last dinner in Franz Josef. Chat with other travellers about their South Island experiences and tips.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hostel
meals.lunch: Packed snacks and sandwiches for the morning hike
meals.dinner: Blue Ice Restaurant in Franz Josef for a slightly more relaxed evening meal (~$20–25 NZD main) or self-cater

day_by_day.notes: Fox Glacier is 25km south of Franz Josef and offers a very similar free valley walk experience — worth visiting if you have time and transport. Both glaciers are retreating rapidly due to climate change, making these visits increasingly significant. Check DOC website (doc.govt.nz) for any track closures due to flooding or rockfall — this is common on the West Coast.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Franz Josef and travel south back toward Queenstown via the scenic West Coast and Haast Pass. Take the Intercity coach (~$50–65 NZD). Enjoy the spectacular coastal scenery along SH6 — rugged Tasman Sea coastline, native bush, and dramatic mountain backdrops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at Knights Point Lookout (free, roadside stop) for stunning Tasman Sea coastal views. Continue through the Haast Pass World Heritage Area. Arrive in Wanaka mid-to-late afternoon. Check in to Wanaka Backpackers (~$35–45 NZD/night dorm).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed evening in Wanaka. Walk the lakefront at sunset — Lake Wanaka at dusk is extraordinarily beautiful. Grab a cheap dinner and rest after the long travel day.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early at Franz Josef hostel before departing
meals.lunch: Packed food for the coach journey — limited stops between Franz Josef and Wanaka
meals.dinner: Francesca's Italian Kitchen in Wanaka for affordable pasta (~$18–22 NZD) or self-cater at hostel

day_by_day.notes: The Haast Pass coach journey is one of New Zealand's great scenic road trips — sit on the right side of the coach heading south for the best views. This is a long travel day (~6 hours total). Book the coach ticket in advance. If sharing a rental car with other travellers, this route is even more flexible and potentially cheaper split 3–4 ways.

day_by_day.morning: Full day in Wanaka. Hike the Roy's Peak Track — one of New Zealand's most photographed hikes (16km return, 1,200m elevation gain, approximately 5–6 hours). Start very early (6:00–7:00am) to avoid crowds and secure the famous ridge-line photo spot. Completely free DOC track.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Roy's Peak descent. The views from the summit over Lake Wanaka, Mount Aspiring National Park, and surrounding peaks are extraordinary on a clear day. Pack plenty of food and water for this full-day hike.
day_by_day.evening: Reward yourself with a well-earned meal in Wanaka town. Visit the quirky Puzzling World (exterior is free to view) or simply relax by the lake and watch the alpenglow on the mountains.

meals.breakfast: Very early self-catered breakfast at hostel before the hike — this is critical
meals.lunch: Packed summit lunch — this is a long exposed hike with no facilities
meals.dinner: Ritual Café or Kai Whakapai in Wanaka for affordable meals (~$18–22 NZD) — you've earned it after Roy's Peak

day_by_day.notes: Roy's Peak is VERY popular in November — start by 6:30am at the latest to beat crowds and secure the iconic ridge photo spot. The track is exposed with no shade — sunscreen, hat, and plenty of water (2L minimum) are essential. The track is closed during lambing season (October 1 – November 10) but should be open by November 24. Verify on DOC website before going.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Wanaka back to Queenstown (1 hour by Ritchies bus or shuttle, ~$20–25 NZD). Arrive in Queenstown and check back in to Nevis Valley Boutique Stay. Take the morning easy — visit the free Queenstown Gardens and recover from Roy's Peak.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Queenstown Hill Time Walk (Te Tapu-nui) — a 2–3 hour return hike from the town centre to the Basket of Dreams sculpture at the summit (907m). Excellent free views over the entire Wakatipu basin. Alternatively, walk the free Tiki Trail up to the Skyline Gondola top station.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Queenstown's bar strip on Beach Street and Cow Lane for the last time. Visit the free waterfront area and enjoy the vibrant atmosphere of this adventure capital.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at Wanaka hostel before departing
meals.lunch: Queenstown — grab a $10–12 NZD wrap or pie from a local café or bakery
meals.dinner: The Cow Restaurant (famous for pizza and fondue, ~$20–25 NZD) or Ferg Bakery for a budget option

day_by_day.notes: If considering a second bungee jump (Nevis Bungy at 134m is the highest in Australasia at ~$275 NZD), today or tomorrow would be the day to book it. The Nevis is significantly more expensive than Kawarau but an entirely different experience. Only consider if budget allows.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day in Queenstown. Take the free Queenstown Trail along the Frankton Arm to Kelvin Heights Peninsula — a beautiful 2–3 hour return walk/cycle with lake and mountain views. Rent a bike from Around the Basin (~$25 NZD/half day) to cover more ground.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the free Queenstown Museum. Browse the Remarkables Market (Saturdays only — if timing aligns) or the weekend arts market. Spend time at the waterfront and take final photos of The Remarkables and Lake Wakatipu. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping at the Queenstown Night Markets or local stores.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Queenstown. Splurge slightly on a final meal to celebrate the trip. Watch the sunset from Queenstown Hill or the waterfront for a stunning final evening in New Zealand.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation — use up remaining groceries
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the Queenstown Trail cycling route
meals.dinner: Treat yourself — Rata Restaurant (mid-range, ~$30–35 NZD main) or a step up from your usual budget for a memorable farewell meal

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to do any final laundry, repack bags, and confirm departure logistics for tomorrow. Check flight details, airport transfer options (Orbus Route 1 to airport is the cheapest at ~$10 NZD), and ensure passport/documents are ready. Purchase any New Zealand souvenirs — Countdown supermarket has affordable local products like Manuka honey and chocolate.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Queenstown. Enjoy a leisurely self-catered breakfast. Take one last walk to the Queenstown waterfront to say goodbye to The Remarkables. Depending on your departure flight time, you may have time for a short final activity — the Queenstown Gardens loop walk (30 minutes, free) is perfect.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Nevis Valley Boutique Stay. Transfer to Queenstown Airport via Orbus public bus Route 1 (~$10 NZD, departs from central Queenstown, journey ~25 minutes). Arrive at the airport at least 2 hours before departure. Grab a final flat white coffee — New Zealand's café culture is world-class.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Queenstown. Reflect on 13 incredible days of hiking, bungee jumping, glacier walks, and South Island adventures.

meals.breakfast: Final self-catered breakfast at accommodation — use up all remaining food
meals.lunch: Airport café or pack remaining snacks for the journey home
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or at your transit airport

day_by_day.notes: Queenstown Airport is small but busy — arrive with plenty of time especially in peak November season. Duty-free purchases are available airside. Declare any food items at customs if transiting through Australia. Total estimated budget for 13 days: NZD $1,800–2,400 per person (including accommodation in dorms/budget stays, transport, activities including one bungy jump, and self-catered meals with occasional restaurant dining). Main splurges: Kawarau Bungy ($175–195), Gondola ($40 one-way), and coach transport between regions.

trip_options.title: Classic New Zealand South Island Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Queenstown Airport at 13:00. Collect luggage, pick up rental car, and drive to Nevis Valley Boutique Stay (~45 min). Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll around the Queenstown lakefront to get oriented and recover from travel.
day_by_day.evening: Explore central Queenstown on foot. Browse the waterfront, enjoy the buzz of the town, and settle in for a relaxed first evening.

meals.breakfast: On the flight or at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at Queenstown Airport — try Vudu Café & Larder for a wholesome sandwich or wrap (~NZD 15–20)
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant on The Mall — mid-range New Zealand cuisine with local lamb and seasonal produce (~NZD 40–55 per person)

day_by_day.notes: No strenuous activities on arrival day. Focus on settling in, hydrating, and adjusting to the time zone. Confirm bookings for Nevis Bungy and Routeburn Track.

day_by_day.morning: Ben Lomond Summit Hike — Start early from the Queenstown Gondola base. Take the gondola up to Skyline and begin the Ben Lomond Track. The hike to the summit (1748m) takes approximately 5–6 hours return and rewards with panoramic views of Lake Wakatipu and the Remarkables.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Ben Lomond Summit Hike descent, arriving back at the gondola mid-afternoon. Rest legs and enjoy the views from Skyline Queenstown before riding the gondola back down.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Queenstown. Light stretching and recovery. Walk along the lakefront at sunset.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or grab a packed lunch from a local deli — Vudu Larder opens early and has great trail food
meals.lunch: Pack your own trail lunch — sandwiches, energy bars, fruit, and plenty of water
meals.dinner: The Cow Restaurant — cozy stone building, excellent pizza and pasta, mid-range pricing (~NZD 25–40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Start the hike no later than 7:30am to allow enough time. Wear layers — summit conditions can be cold and windy even in November. Bring sunscreen, trekking poles optional but helpful.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery morning — sleep in slightly. Light breakfast and a gentle walk along the Queenstown Gardens (flat, lakeside, beautiful in late spring). Visit the rose garden and enjoy the calm before the big jump tomorrow.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive the scenic Crown Range Road to Arrowtown (~25 min). Explore this charming gold-rush era village, walk the Arrow River trail, and visit the Lakes District Museum for local history.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown. Enjoy dinner and an early night to prepare for the Nevis Bungy tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or nearby — try Bespoke Kitchen in Queenstown for healthy bowls and coffee (~NZD 18–25)
meals.lunch: Arrowtown — Provisions of Arrowtown, a beloved local café with excellent sandwiches and cabinet food (~NZD 15–22)
meals.dinner: Fergburger — Queenstown's iconic burger institution, great value and unmissable (~NZD 15–20)

day_by_day.notes: Rest day is intentional before the Nevis Bungy. Stay well hydrated and avoid alcohol the night before the jump. Confirm your Nevis Bungy time slot — typically morning departures from Queenstown base.

day_by_day.morning: Nevis Bungy Jump — New Zealand's highest bungy at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. Check in at the AJ Hackett base in Queenstown town centre, take the 4WD transfer to the Nevis Valley pod, and take the ultimate leap. The experience includes the transfer, harness fitting, and jump (~3 hours total).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Queenstown by early afternoon. Adrenaline comedown — relax at the hotel, review your jump photos and video package, and take a gentle lakeside walk.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your jump with a nice dinner out. Share stories with fellow travelers.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the jump — avoid heavy meals. Toast, fruit, and coffee at the hotel
meals.lunch: Post-jump celebration lunch at Queenstown — Botswana Butchery for a treat, or Pub on Wharf for casual lakeside dining (~NZD 25–40)
meals.dinner: Wai Restaurant at Hilton Queenstown — lakeside views, modern New Zealand cuisine, mid-range splurge to celebrate (~NZD 45–60 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Nevis Bungy costs approximately NZD 275 per person. Must be pre-booked. Weight limit applies (45–130kg). Do not eat a heavy meal within 2 hours of the jump. Photos and video are available for purchase on the day.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Queenstown to Te Anau (~2 hours) — the gateway to Fiordland. Arrive and check in at mid-range accommodation in Te Anau. Visit the Te Anau Glowworm Caves (book in advance) — a magical underground cave system with glowworms accessible only by boat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Te Anau township and the lakefront. Walk the Te Anau Lakefront Track (easy, flat, 3km return) and enjoy views of the Fiordland mountains across the lake.
day_by_day.evening: Early dinner and rest — tomorrow is the Milford Sound day trip, requiring an early start.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at hotel in Queenstown before departure, or stop at a café in Kingston on the drive
meals.lunch: Redcliff Restaurant & Bar in Te Anau — local wild game and South Island produce (~NZD 25–38)
meals.dinner: Miles Better Pies or The Fat Duck in Te Anau — casual, affordable, great for a pre-hike evening (~NZD 15–30)

day_by_day.notes: Te Anau Glowworm Caves must be pre-booked through Real Journeys (~NZD 55 per adult). This is a 2-hour experience. Accommodation in Te Anau: Kingsgate Hotel Te Anau or similar mid-range option (~NZD 130–180/night).

day_by_day.morning: Early departure from Te Anau (6:30am) for the scenic 2-hour drive to Milford Sound along SH94. Stop at The Chasm and Mirror Lakes for short walks and photos en route. Arrive at Milford Sound and board a scenic cruise (~2 hours) to see Mitre Peak, waterfalls, and wildlife.
day_by_day.afternoon: Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo — After the cruise, join the afternoon kayak session paddling the fiord's calm waters beneath towering cliffs. Combine with a short guided hike on the Milford foreshore track for the full experience (~3–4 hours).
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Te Anau (~2 hours). Arrive early evening, tired but exhilarated.

meals.breakfast: Very early breakfast at hotel before 6:30am departure — pack snacks for the drive
meals.lunch: Pack your own lunch or purchase from the Milford Sound Lodge café — limited options at Milford so bring food
meals.dinner: Sandfly Café in Te Anau — relaxed atmosphere, good pizza and pasta, well-priced (~NZD 20–30)

day_by_day.notes: Milford Sound Kayak & Hike Combo costs approximately NZD 195–220 per person. Book well in advance — this is a popular experience. Wear waterproof layers for kayaking. The drive to Milford is one of the most scenic in the world — allow extra time for photo stops.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning in Te Anau. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely breakfast, and prepare gear for the Routeburn Track starting tomorrow. Visit the Fiordland National Park Visitor Centre to get the latest track conditions and weather forecast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Short optional hike: Kepler Track Day Walk from Te Anau (Luxmore Hut section — 3–4 hours return to the bush edge, easy-moderate). Great for stretching legs without overexerting before the multi-day hike.
day_by_day.evening: Final gear check and pack for the Routeburn Track (2 nights on the track). Lay out and organize everything needed. Ensure hut passes are confirmed.

meals.breakfast: Café Mossburn or The Ranch Bar & Grill in Te Anau — full cooked breakfast to fuel up (~NZD 18–28)
meals.lunch: Light lunch from a local supermarket in Te Anau — stock up on trail food for the Routeburn here
meals.dinner: Ristorante Pizzeria da Tano in Te Anau — authentic Italian, generous portions, great pre-hike carb load (~NZD 25–38)

day_by_day.notes: Purchase all Routeburn Track hut passes through DOC (Department of Conservation) in advance — approximately NZD 75 per night per person. Pack light but include: rain gear, warm layers, first aid kit, headlamp, and enough food for 2 nights on the track.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Te Anau to Routeburn Shelter trailhead near Glenorchy (~1.5 hours via Queenstown). Begin the Routeburn Track from the Routeburn end. Hike through stunning beech forest to the Routeburn Flats Hut (~2 hours, 7.5km). Enjoy the open river flats and mountain views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue from Routeburn Flats to Routeburn Falls Hut (~1.5 hours, 2.5km). The trail climbs steeply through forest to emerge above the treeline at the dramatic Routeburn Falls. Arrive at the hut (~1000m elevation) with stunning alpine views.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into Routeburn Falls Hut (DOC hut, 48 bunks). Cook dinner in the communal kitchen, socialize with fellow trampers, and enjoy the spectacular alpine sunset over the Harris Mountains.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Te Anau accommodation before departure
meals.lunch: Trail lunch packed from Te Anau — wraps, cheese, crackers, nuts, dried fruit
meals.dinner: Self-cooked hut meal — bring freeze-dried meals or prepare pasta/rice with packaged sauces on hut gas cookers

day_by_day.notes: Leave car at Routeburn Shelter car park (secure). The track is well-marked but weather can change rapidly — always carry rain gear. Routeburn Falls Hut has gas cookers, water, and toilets but no showers. November is peak season — expect other hikers.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Routeburn Falls Hut early. Hike the spectacular Harris Saddle section — the highlight of the entire track. Cross the alpine saddle at 1255m with 360-degree views of Fiordland and Mount Aspiring National Parks. Optional side trip to Conical Hill summit (30 min return) for even more dramatic panoramas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from Harris Saddle through the stunning Lake Mackenzie basin. Arrive at Lake Mackenzie Hut (~4 hours from Routeburn Falls, 11km). Relax by the turquoise alpine lake, take a refreshing dip if weather permits, and enjoy the dramatic mountain backdrop.
day_by_day.evening: Overnight at Lake Mackenzie Hut (DOC hut, 50 bunks). This is one of the most scenic hut locations in New Zealand. Watch the alpenglow on the surrounding peaks at sunset.

meals.breakfast: Self-cooked at Routeburn Falls Hut — oats, muesli, or instant porridge with dried fruit and coffee
meals.lunch: Trail lunch on the track — eat at Harris Saddle for the best lunch view in New Zealand
meals.dinner: Self-cooked at Lake Mackenzie Hut — freeze-dried meal or packaged pasta/noodle dish

day_by_day.notes: Harris Saddle can be extremely windy and cold — pack extra warm layers even in November. The descent to Lake Mackenzie is steep in sections. Total hiking distance today: approximately 11km, 5–6 hours. Stay hydrated throughout.

day_by_day.morning: Final day on the Routeburn Track. Depart Lake Mackenzie Hut and hike the remaining section to The Divide on SH94 (~3 hours, 8.5km). The trail passes through beautiful beech forest and the Earland Falls viewpoint (174m waterfall — spectacular).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at The Divide. Take the pre-arranged shuttle back to your car at Routeburn Shelter (book through Tracknet, ~NZD 45 per person). Drive back to Queenstown (~1.5 hours). Check back into Nevis Valley Boutique Stay. Hot shower — pure bliss after 3 days on the track.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory dinner in Queenstown to mark completing the Routeburn Track.

meals.breakfast: Self-cooked at Lake Mackenzie Hut — use up remaining trail food
meals.lunch: Pack the last of your trail snacks for the final section — there are no facilities at The Divide
meals.dinner: Flame Bar & Grill Queenstown — celebrate with a proper South Island steak or lamb rack, mid-range treat (~NZD 40–55 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the Tracknet shuttle from The Divide to Routeburn Shelter before starting the track. Do laundry this evening — most accommodation has laundry facilities. Rest well; you've earned it.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day in Queenstown. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast. Visit the Queenstown Farmers Market (held at Earnslaw Park on Saturdays — if timing aligns) or browse local shops. Light walk along the lakefront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional: Take the Queenstown Gondola up to Skyline for panoramic views (no hiking today — just the gondola ride). Enjoy the luge track for a fun, low-impact activity (~NZD 45 for 3 rides). Alternatively, visit Gibbston Valley Winery (~30 min drive) for a cellar door tasting of Central Otago Pinot Noir (~NZD 10–15 tasting fee).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a lakeside bar. Final evening in the Queenstown area.

meals.breakfast: Bespoke Kitchen or Vudu Café — treat yourself to eggs benedict or a smoothie bowl (~NZD 18–28)
meals.lunch: Gibbston Valley Winery Restaurant if visiting — wood-fired pizza and local produce in a stunning gorge setting (~NZD 25–38)
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant — chef Josh Emmett's flagship, celebrating New Zealand produce. Book ahead (~NZD 45–65 per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberate rest day between the Routeburn Track and the Franz Josef journey tomorrow. Use the afternoon to sort gear, repack, and plan the drive north. Gibbston Valley is a highlight of Central Otago wine country — highly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Queenstown early and drive north along the West Coast — one of New Zealand's most dramatic drives. Route: Queenstown → Wanaka → Haast Pass → Fox Glacier (~5 hours total). Stop at Blue Pools near Makarora for a short 45-minute return walk to brilliant turquoise glacier-fed pools.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue driving north past Fox Glacier to Franz Josef (~45 min further). Check in to mid-range accommodation in Franz Josef township. Rest and freshen up after the long drive.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Franz Josef village. It's a small township with a few restaurants and bars — perfect for a relaxed evening before the glacier walk tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel in Queenstown before departure
meals.lunch: Pack lunch from Queenstown or stop at the Haast township café (limited options on this route — bring food)
meals.dinner: Alice May Restaurant in Franz Josef — local venison, lamb, and seafood, cozy atmosphere (~NZD 30–45 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Haast Pass drive is spectacular but long — allow extra time for stops at Thunder Creek Falls and the Gates of Haast. Accommodation in Franz Josef: Rainforest Retreat or Scenic Hotel Franz Josef Glacier (~NZD 140–200/night). Fill up on petrol before leaving Wanaka — limited fuel options on the West Coast.

day_by_day.morning: Franz Josef Glacier Valley Walk — Join a guided walk through the dramatic terminal valley of Franz Josef Glacier. Hike across ancient glacial moraine, through rainforest, and as close to the active glacier face as conditions permit. The guided walk takes approximately 3–4 hours and provides incredible geological and ecological insight (~NZD 79–95 per person).
day_by_day.afternoon: After the glacier walk, drive north to Hokitika or continue to Greymouth for flight connections, or begin the return journey south depending on departure logistics. If time allows, stop at Hokitika Gorge (~30 min detour) for a short walk to see the impossibly blue glacial river gorge — a perfect final South Island memory.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening celebration dinner. Reflect on 13 incredible days — bungy jumping, multiple Great Walks, fiords, glaciers, and everything in between.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Franz Josef accommodation — fuel up for the glacier walk
meals.lunch: Post-walk lunch at Speight's Landing Bar & Café in Franz Josef — burgers, nachos, casual and affordable (~NZD 18–28)
meals.dinner: Final night dinner — if in Hokitika, try Stella Café & Bar for local whitebait fritters (a West Coast specialty) and a glass of Central Otago Pinot Noir (~NZD 30–45 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Franz Josef Glacier is actively retreating — the guided valley walk gets you as close as safely possible. Helicopter glacier landings are available as an upgrade (~NZD 350+) if budget allows. Check departure logistics carefully — if flying from Queenstown, allow a full driving day to return south. Consider one-way car rental if flying from Christchurch instead.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium New Zealand South Island Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Take the ultimate leap from New Zealand's highest bungy jump at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. This iconic AJ Hackett experience offers breathtaking views of the Remarkables mountain range and an adrenaline rush like no other. The jump includes a scenic gondola ride to the suspended pod over the canyon.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Multi-Day Hike
experiences.description: Trek one of New Zealand's Great Walks through pristine alpine scenery connecting Fiordland and Mount Aspiring National Parks. The 32km trail features dramatic mountain passes, glacier-carved valleys, and stunning views of Lake Mackenzie. Huts are available along the route for overnight stays, making it perfect for a 2-3 day adventure.

experiences.name: Franz Josef Glacier Valley Walk
experiences.description: Hike through the dramatic terminal valley of Franz Josef Glacier, one of the world's most accessible glaciers descending into a temperate rainforest. The self-guided valley walk takes you to stunning glacier viewpoints with towering ice walls and turquoise meltwater streams. Rangers provide safety briefings and the trail is well-marked with multiple lookout points.

experiences.name: Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo
experiences.description: Paddle through the majestic fiords of Milford Sound while surrounded by towering peaks, cascading waterfalls, and abundant wildlife including dolphins and seals. Combine the kayaking experience with a guided walk along the Milford foreshore track for a full day of immersive nature adventure. The experience includes equipment, guides, and stunning views of Mitre Peak.

experiences.name: Ben Lomond Summit Hike
experiences.description: Conquer the iconic Ben Lomond peak rising 1748 meters above Queenstown for panoramic views of Lake Wakatipu, the Remarkables, and surrounding mountain ranges. The challenging 11km return trail begins through beech forest before opening into dramatic alpine terrain above the treeline. Take the Skyline Gondola up to shorten the ascent and save energy for the summit push.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Private airport transfer to Queenstown Boutique Stay in Nevis Valley. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely orientation walk around the boutique property grounds. Enjoy a welcome glass of Central Otago Pinot Noir on arrival.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into Queenstown for a relaxed first evening. Stroll along the Queenstown waterfront and Lake Wakatipu at golden hour. Enjoy a private sunset cocktail experience arranged by the hotel before dinner.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight
meals.lunch: Light in-flight meal or grab a premium bite at Queenstown Airport's departure lounge café upon landing
meals.dinner: Botswana Butchery, Queenstown — a celebrated lakeside fine-dining restaurant known for premium South Island lamb, aged beef, and an exceptional Central Otago wine list. Reserve a window table for lake views.

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day — keep the pace gentle to recover from long-haul travel. Confirm all upcoming activity bookings with the hotel concierge this evening. Jet lag management: stay awake until at least 21:00 local time.

day_by_day.morning: Ben Lomond Summit Hike — begin the ascent early from the Queenstown gondola base or take the gondola up to Skyline to save elevation. The trail climbs through tussock and alpine terrain to the 1,748m summit with sweeping panoramic views of Lake Wakatipu, The Remarkables, and Cecil Peak. Allow 5–6 hours round trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend Ben Lomond and return to the hotel for a recovery soak and spa treatment. The boutique stay's private amenities or a nearby luxury spa (Eforea Spa at Hilton Queenstown) offer massage and hydrotherapy to ease tired muscles.
day_by_day.evening: Scenic gondola ride back up to Skyline Queenstown for dinner above the city lights and lake.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the boutique hotel — eggs benedict, freshly baked pastries, local fruit, and barista coffee before the hike
meals.lunch: Packed premium trail lunch prepared by the hotel — artisan sandwiches, local cheeses, bliss balls, and a thermos of hot tea
meals.dinner: Stratosfare Restaurant at Skyline Queenstown — buffet-style fine dining with panoramic night views of Queenstown and Lake Wakatipu; premium wine pairing available

day_by_day.notes: Wear layered merino wool clothing for Ben Lomond — summit temperatures can be 10–15°C cooler than town even in November. Start no later than 07:30 to avoid afternoon cloud build-up at the summit. Trekking poles strongly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Nevis Bungy Jump — the ultimate adrenaline experience. Transfer to the Nevis Bungy platform via 4WD vehicle through the dramatic Nevis Valley gorge. At 134 meters, this is New Zealand's highest bungy jump, suspended above the turquoise Nevis River. Optional tandem jump available. Full AJ Hackett premium experience with video and photo package.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Queenstown and unwind with a private e-bike tour along the Queenstown Trail along Lake Hayes and the Arrow River — a gentle, scenic contrast to the morning's intensity. Alternatively, enjoy a wine tasting tour of the nearby Gibbston Valley wineries by private vehicle.
day_by_day.evening: Luxury wine and cheese evening at a Gibbston Valley cellar door (Peregrine Wines or Amisfield) with a curated tasting of Central Otago Pinot Noir, Riesling, and Pinot Gris.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — high-protein start with smoked salmon, avocado, eggs, and fresh juice before the bungy
meals.lunch: Amisfield Winery Bistro, Lake Hayes — celebrated farm-to-table cuisine with a 'Trust the Chef' seasonal menu and stunning vineyard views
meals.dinner: The Bunker, Queenstown — intimate, award-winning restaurant in a historic stone building; exceptional tasting menu with New Zealand game, seafood, and curated wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Nevis Bungy weight limits: 45kg–127kg. Avoid heavy meals at least 2 hours before the jump. The hotel concierge should pre-book the Nevis Bungy well in advance as slots fill quickly in peak season (November). Video and photo package is highly recommended as a keepsake.

day_by_day.morning: Private scenic helicopter flight from Queenstown over The Remarkables, Fiordland, and Milford Sound — a premium aerial perspective of the South Island's most dramatic landscapes. Many operators (Glacier Southern Lakes Helicopters) offer 45–90 minute scenic flights with optional glacier or remote alpine landing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or transfer to Glenorchy (45 minutes from Queenstown) — a stunning lakeside village at the head of Lake Wakatipu used as a filming location for Lord of the Rings. Walk the Glenorchy Lagoon Boardwalk and Paradise Nature Reserve. Explore the iconic braided river flats and Dart River valley.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown for a relaxed evening at leisure. Optional visit to Queenstown's premium whisky bar or cocktail lounge.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — leisurely start before the helicopter flight
meals.lunch: Glenorchy Cafe — a beloved local institution with hearty New Zealand fare; try the venison pie or salmon bagel
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant, Queenstown — Chef Josh Emett's flagship restaurant celebrating New Zealand produce with refined, creative cuisine. Book the chef's tasting menu with wine flight.

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter flights are weather-dependent — have the concierge arrange a flexible booking with a weather guarantee or rebooking option. Glenorchy road is unsealed in parts; a 4WD or private driver is recommended for comfort.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Queenstown early by private vehicle or scenic drive to Te Anau (2.5 hours) — the gateway to Fiordland National Park. Check in to a premium Te Anau lodge (Fiordland Lodge recommended for its stunning lake and mountain views). Visit the Te Anau Glowworm Caves by boat — a magical underground limestone cave system lit by thousands of glowworms.
day_by_day.afternoon: Afternoon scenic cruise on Lake Te Anau with a private charter operator. Explore the remote, mist-shrouded arms of the lake surrounded by ancient beech forest and Fiordland peaks.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset from the Fiordland Lodge deck with aperitifs, watching the alpenglow on the Murchison Mountains across the lake.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast at Queenstown Boutique Stay before departure
meals.lunch: Redcliff Restaurant, Te Anau — a local favourite in a charming heritage cottage; try the venison or fresh Fiordland whitebait
meals.dinner: In-lodge dining at Fiordland Lodge — private chef dinner with locally sourced Fiordland venison, Bluff oysters (in season), and Central Otago wines by the fireplace

day_by_day.notes: Book Te Anau Glowworm Caves well in advance — Real Journeys operates the tours and they sell out in peak season. The drive from Queenstown to Te Anau via State Highway 6 is spectacular; consider stopping at Kingston for lake views.

day_by_day.morning: Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo — depart Te Anau early for the iconic 2-hour drive to Milford Sound through the Homer Tunnel and Fiordland's ancient valleys. Begin the guided kayak experience on the fiord, paddling beneath Mitre Peak (1,692m) and past thundering waterfalls including Stirling Falls. The fiord is at its most magical in morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the combo experience with a guided hike along the Milford foreshore and into the surrounding rainforest. Spot fur seals, dolphins, and rare Fiordland crested penguins. Optional Milford Sound cruise upgrade for an extended fiord experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return drive to Te Anau (2 hours). Arrive in time for a relaxing soak and dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early packed gourmet breakfast from the lodge — consumed en route to Milford Sound
meals.lunch: Packed premium lunch provided by the kayak/hike operator, enjoyed on the fiord foreshore with Mitre Peak as your backdrop
meals.dinner: Sandfly Bar & Restaurant, Te Anau — relaxed, quality dining with Fiordland salmon, craft beers, and a warm atmosphere after a big adventure day

day_by_day.notes: The Milford Road is one of the world's great scenic drives — allow time for stops at Mirror Lakes, The Chasm, and the Avenue of the Disappearing Mountain. Depart Te Anau by 07:00 to beat tour bus traffic at Milford. Sandflies are aggressive at Milford — bring premium insect repellent and long sleeves.

day_by_day.morning: Routeburn Track Multi-Day Hike — Day 1. Private guided transfer to the Routeburn Track trailhead at The Divide (accessed via Te Anau and Milford Road). Begin the Great Walk heading toward Lake Mackenzie, passing through ancient podocarp forest, open river flats, and climbing through alpine meadows. Distance: approximately 11km to Lake Mackenzie Hut.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Lake Mackenzie — one of the most spectacular hut locations in New Zealand, perched above a glacial lake surrounded by towering peaks. Settle into premium guided accommodation (Ultimate Hikes' guided Routeburn with lodge-style huts and private rooms).
day_by_day.evening: Guided naturalist talk at Lake Mackenzie Lodge about Fiordland's ecology, geology, and birdlife. Spot kea (alpine parrots) around the hut at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast at Fiordland Lodge before transfer to trailhead
meals.lunch: Trail lunch pack — gourmet wraps, energy bars, fruit, and hot drinks from thermos
meals.dinner: Communal lodge dinner at Lake Mackenzie Hut (Ultimate Hikes provides excellent hot meals) — hearty New Zealand lamb stew, fresh bread, and dessert

day_by_day.notes: Book the Routeburn Track through Ultimate Hikes for the guided lodge experience — this is the premium option with private rooms, hot showers, and cooked meals rather than basic DOC huts. Booking essential many months in advance. Pack only essentials in a daypack; Ultimate Hikes manages luggage transfers.

day_by_day.morning: Routeburn Track — Day 2. Early morning walk from Lake Mackenzie up to Harris Saddle (1,255m) — the high point of the track with extraordinary 360-degree views across Fiordland and Mount Aspiring National Park. Optional side trip to Conical Hill (add 1 hour) for even more expansive panoramas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from Harris Saddle through the Routeburn Flats, passing the Routeburn Falls and Falls Hut. Arrive at Routeburn Flats Hut/Lodge area. Distance: approximately 14km. The valley scenery is among the finest in the Southern Alps.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at Routeburn Flats Lodge. Wildlife spotting for whio (blue duck) along the Routeburn River at dusk — one of New Zealand's rarest birds.

meals.breakfast: Hot lodge breakfast at Lake Mackenzie — porridge, eggs, toast, and coffee before the big climb to Harris Saddle
meals.lunch: Trail lunch at Harris Saddle — enjoy the views while eating from your gourmet trail pack
meals.dinner: Hot lodge dinner at Routeburn Flats — roasted chicken, seasonal vegetables, and warm pudding

day_by_day.notes: Harris Saddle can be exposed and cold even in November — pack a wind shell, gloves, and beanie regardless of morning weather. The climb from Lake Mackenzie to Harris Saddle is the most demanding section of the track; take it slowly and enjoy the views. Weather changes rapidly — follow guide advice on Conical Hill side trip.

day_by_day.morning: Routeburn Track — Day 3 (final day). Morning walk from Routeburn Flats through the spectacular lower valley to the Routeburn Shelter trailhead near Glenorchy. Distance: approximately 9km. The valley floor section winds through ancient red and silver beech forest with crystal-clear river crossings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private vehicle transfer from Routeburn trailhead back to Queenstown (1.5 hours via Glenorchy). Return to Queenstown Boutique Stay in Nevis Valley for a well-deserved luxury recovery afternoon — spa treatment, bath, and rest.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory post-Routeburn dinner in Queenstown to mark the completion of one of New Zealand's greatest Great Walks.

meals.breakfast: Final lodge breakfast at Routeburn Flats before the last day's walk
meals.lunch: Glenorchy Cafe stop en route back to Queenstown — pie, coffee, and a well-earned sweet treat
meals.dinner: Jervois Steak House, Queenstown — premium aged New Zealand beef, excellent wine cellar, and a celebratory atmosphere to mark the completion of the Routeburn Track

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private transfer pickup from Routeburn Shelter in advance — the trailhead is remote. Ultimate Hikes typically organises return transport as part of the guided package. Use the afternoon spa session to book in advance with the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at the Queenstown Boutique Stay. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast, and take a gentle walk around the Nevis Valley property. Optional yoga or stretching session to recover from the multi-day hike.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private jet boat experience on the Shotover River — Shotover Jet offers an exhilarating 25-minute ride through dramatic canyon walls at high speed. Alternatively, explore Arrowtown — a beautifully preserved 1860s gold rush village 20 minutes from Queenstown — visiting the Lakes District Museum and boutique galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset wine tasting at Peregrine Wines, Gibbston Valley — one of Central Otago's most architecturally stunning wineries with a curved schist-stone cellar door. Private tasting of their flagship Pinot Noir and Riesling.

meals.breakfast: Luxurious late hotel breakfast — full cooked spread, fresh pastries, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Provisions of Arrowtown — an acclaimed café in the historic village with exceptional seasonal menus, local produce, and outstanding coffee
meals.dinner: Saffron Restaurant, Arrowtown — Central Otago's most celebrated fine-dining destination in a historic stone building; seasonal tasting menu with local venison, salmon, and truffles

day_by_day.notes: Day 10 is intentionally lighter in pace to allow full physical recovery from the Routeburn Track. Arrowtown is one of New Zealand's most charming historic towns — allow at least 2 hours to wander the Chinese Settlement, heritage main street, and riverside walk.

day_by_day.morning: Private scenic drive north from Queenstown toward the West Coast via the Haast Pass — one of New Zealand's most dramatic mountain crossings through Mount Aspiring National Park. Stop at Thunder Creek Falls, Blue Pools (short walk to turquoise glacial pools), and Gates of Haast gorge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Franz Josef Glacier Village (approximately 4–4.5 hours from Queenstown). Check in to The Terrace Motels & Chalets or Te Waonui Forest Retreat (the region's most luxurious eco-lodge). Franz Josef Glacier Valley Walk — a guided afternoon hike through the dramatic terminal valley of the glacier, past ancient moraines, ice caves, and braided glacial rivers to the glacier face viewpoint.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at Te Waonui Forest Retreat with canopy views of the temperate rainforest and the sounds of native birdsong.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Queenstown Boutique Stay before the long scenic drive
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch stop at Blue Pools, Haast Pass — enjoy premium packed lunch from the hotel amid stunning beech forest and turquoise water
meals.dinner: Forest Floor Restaurant at Te Waonui Forest Retreat — multi-course West Coast dining featuring whitebait, blue cod, venison, and West Coast cream; surrounded by rainforest with floor-to-ceiling windows

day_by_day.notes: The Haast Pass drive is approximately 4 hours — depart Queenstown by 08:30 to arrive at Franz Josef with time for the afternoon glacier walk. The Haast Pass road (SH6) is fully sealed but narrow in places. Fill up with fuel in Wanaka before crossing the pass as petrol stations are scarce. Franz Josef weather is notoriously changeable — pack full waterproofs.

day_by_day.morning: Franz Josef Glacier Heli-Hike — the ultimate glacier experience. Helicopter flight from Franz Josef Village onto the upper snowfields of the Franz Josef or Fox Glacier, landing at 2,000+ meters altitude. Guided 3-hour hike through ice caves, seracs, crevasses, and blue ice formations with expert glacier guides. Crampons and equipment provided.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the village by helicopter. Afternoon at leisure — visit the West Coast Wildlife Centre to see kiwi and tuatara up close in a world-class facility. Alternatively, take a forest walk through the Tatare Tunnels or Sentinel Rock Lookout Track.
day_by_day.evening: Final West Coast evening — enjoy a private stargazing experience if skies are clear (the West Coast offers exceptional dark skies away from light pollution).

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Te Waonui Forest Retreat before the heli-hike — high energy meal essential
meals.lunch: Alice May Restaurant, Franz Josef — casual but quality West Coast dining with excellent burgers, fish, and craft beer after the glacier adventure
meals.dinner: Final dinner at Te Waonui's Forest Floor Restaurant — request a special farewell tasting menu with West Coast Pinot Noir and Chardonnay pairings

day_by_day.notes: The Franz Josef Heli-Hike is weather-dependent — operators (Franz Josef Glacier Guides) will advise on the morning. Have a backup activity planned (Valley Walk extension or West Coast Wildlife Centre). This is one of the most extraordinary experiences available in New Zealand and worth every effort to complete. Book well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on the West Coast — take a peaceful sunrise walk through the Waiho River flats with views of the glacier valley in morning light. Visit the historic St James Anglican Church — a tiny chapel with a famous glacier view through its window, one of New Zealand's most photographed scenes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scenic drive south or arrange a private scenic flight back to Queenstown or Christchurch for onward travel. If driving, the return via Haast Pass offers equally stunning scenery with different light. Final stop at Lake Wanaka for lunch and a lakeside walk before continuing to Queenstown.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Queenstown or departure lounge depending on flight schedule. If overnight remains, celebrate the journey's end with a premium dinner and Queenstown's vibrant atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely final breakfast at Te Waonui Forest Retreat — savour the rainforest setting one last time
meals.lunch: Francesca's Italian Kitchen, Wanaka — exceptional Italian cuisine with local ingredients in one of New Zealand's most beautiful lakeside towns
meals.dinner: If remaining in Queenstown: Amisfield Winery & Bistro for a final celebratory dinner with Central Otago's finest wines, or departure lounge dining at Queenstown Airport

day_by_day.notes: Confirm return flights and transfers on this final day well in advance. If flying from Franz Josef, Sounds Air operates scenic flights to Queenstown and Christchurch — a spectacular final aerial view of the Southern Alps, glaciers, and Fiordland. Allow extra time at Queenstown Airport as it can be busy in peak season. Purchase final New Zealand souvenirs — Merino wool, Manuka honey, and Central Otago wines make excellent gifts.

query: New Zealand South Island, $4000, hiking and bungee jumping, November 2026
